repos_data.description: Fundamentally a swig/python wrapper around Peter Jaeckel's lets_be_rational.  lets_be_rational focuses exclusively on Black76, while Vollib extends this to add support for Black-Scholes and Black-Scholes-Merton.
A python implementation of the fast-reversion Heston model of Mechkov [2015, https://goo.gl/2awbrV], for FX purposes.
vanilla-option-pricers - Numba-vectorised Black-Scholes-Merton and Bachelier prices, Greeks, and implied-volatility fits over NumPy arrays for quantitative research pipelines
A Python implementation of the rough Bergomi model.
An libary to price financial options written in Python. Includes: Black Scholes, Black 76, Implied Volatility, American, European, Asian, Spread Options
Python SDK for the FlashAlpha options analytics API — live options screener, gamma exposure (GEX), DEX/VEX/CHEX, options flow, 0DTE, VRP, volatility surfaces, greeks
Gatheral SVI vol surface — raw/natural/jump-wings, butterfly & calendar arbitrage checks, calibration. Zero dependencies.
This repository contains codes that were executed during my training in the CQF (Certificate in Quantitative Finance). The codes are organized by class, facilitating navigation and reference.
A complete set of volatility estimators based on Euan Sinclair's Volatility Trading
The SABR stochastic-vol model — Hagan 2002 lognormal & normal implied vol, Obloj correction, smile calibration. Matches QuantLib. Zero deps.

repo_meta_data.description: Demo code for direct Black-Scholes implied-volatility calculation from normalized call prices via the inverse-Gaussian quantile representation.
